title: Project: a support-message classifier
summary: Train a tiny text classifier, evaluate held-out messages, and inspect its errors.

sections.title: Build a complete baseline
paragraphs: This project uses multinomial Naive Bayes. Each class has a prior based on its training frequency and a distribution over vocabulary words. Add-one smoothing keeps observed-vocabulary words from getting zero probability in a class.

For a query, sum the log prior and word log probabilities, then choose the highest score. Summing logs avoids underflow from multiplying many small numbers. The conditional-independence assumption is a simplification; correlated words are treated as separate evidence.

sections.title: Evaluate honestly
paragraphs: The dataset is deliberately small and invented. It demonstrates a full training-to-inference path, not a production support classifier. Unknown words are ignored, so a query with no known terms falls back to review.

The selected class score is not a calibrated probability. Inspect missed synonyms, mixed-topic messages, negation, and unknown language. Expand the labeling guide and evaluation set before adding complexity. Keep any final test examples out of vocabulary construction and tuning.

code.explanation: The script learns word counts only from the four training messages. The refund example intentionally reveals a missing concept in the vocabulary.

practice.goal: Extend the classifier without contaminating its evaluation.
steps: Create a separate development set with mixed topics and unfamiliar wording.
Add original training messages for missing concepts, then freeze the vocabulary.
Evaluate once on a new held-out set and write a short model card with counts and failures.
practice.solution: Use development errors to improve training coverage. Do not report the repeatedly inspected four-case fixture as an unbiased final score. Keep no-known-word queries in review and consider an ambiguity rule validated on separate examples.
practice.expected: The initial script gets 3 of 4 held-out fixture cases correct; refund request is sent to review.

quiz.question: Why build the vocabulary only from training text?
options: To preserve an independent evaluation boundary
Because test text is never useful for error analysis
quiz.explanation: Evaluation inputs should not influence the learned representation before the final evaluation. Error analysis comes after the measured run.
